info.title: Filinq
info.description:
The JSON API of Filinq, document management for Nextcloud: anonymisation of documents and folders, signing, templates, archiving and retention, legal holds, settings and the setup wizard. The documents' metadata objects are stored in OpenRegister and read and written through its API; this document covers the endpoints Filinq adds on top.

Every path is served under `/api/v1/`, the version this document describes. The unversioned `/api/` paths keep working, are deprecated, and name their `/api/v1/` successor in a `Link` header next to a `Deprecation` header. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`), and every response carries an `API-Version` header. Paths that implement an external standard keep the formats of that standard and are not described here; where this app documents them, openapi.standards.json does.

post.summary: Anonymize entities in a document  Replaces detected entities in the document with anonymized placeholders
post.description: Anonymize entities in a document  Replaces detected entities in the document with anonymized placeholders. Supports optional excludeTypes, minConfidence, appendBasisSummary, and outputFormat parameters. Stray `bases[]` fields on entity entries are silently ignored (per 2026-05-12 explore-mode rework); bases are set via OR's PATCH /api/entity-relations/{id}.

post.summary: Create an anonymization batch from an existing Nextcloud folder
post.description: Accepts either a folder ID or a folder path (exactly one). When `folderId` is provided, the folder is resolved via Nextcloud's file system by node ID; if the ID maps to multiple mounts in the user's tree, a mount with write permission is preferred over a read-only one. When `folderPath` is provided, the existing path-based lookup is used. The resulting batch stores (and the response returns) both `folderId` and `folderPath` regardless of which input was supplied.

200.description: Batch created; background extraction has been queued.

folderPath.description: Human-readable folder path, resolved at batch creation time.

400.description: Invalid input — neither `folderId` nor `folderPath` provided, both provided, the resolved node is not a folder, the folder is empty, or the folder exceeds the configured maximum batch size.

404.description: Folder not found for the given `folderId` or `folderPath`.

folderId.description: Nextcloud node ID of the folder to batch.

folderPath.description: Path of the folder relative to the user's root.

post.description: Accept a multipart upload and create a new anonymization batch.

put.summary: Persist a new WOO anonymization profile from the request body
put.description: Persist a new WOO anonymization profile from the request body.  ADMIN-ONLY, DELIBERATELY. The profile this writes is INSTANCE-WIDE: it lands in `IAppConfig` under `filinq_woo_entity_profiles` (`WooProfileService::saveProfile()`), and `EntityConsolidationService` reads it to decide which entity types are redacted for EVERY user. Moving `PERSON` / `BSN` / `EMAIL` out of the `anonymize` set therefore leaves other people's PII in place on every subsequent run.  ⚠️ The obvious way to satisfy a "missing auth attribute" finding here, copying the sibling `getProfiles()`'s user-level annotation onto this method, WOULD INTRODUCE EXACTLY THAT VULNERABILITY. The two are not symmetric: reading the profile is a user-level concern, writing it is instance policy. Until this attribute existed the endpoint was admin-only only by ACCIDENT (Nextcloud defaults an unannotated method to admin), and the body's lone `getUser() === null` check reads as though user-level access were intended, which is what makes the wrong fix look right.  `#[AuthorizedAdminSetting]` matches how every other instance-wide write in this app declares itself (`SettingsController`, `AnonymiserWarningController`).  The null-session check below is retained as defence in depth, not as the authorization boundary, the attribute is the boundary.

200.description: Success message, or an error payload when the body is malformed.

patch.summary: Record a per-entity skip/include decision, guarded by the prohibition policy
patch.description: Record a per-entity skip/include decision, guarded by the prohibition policy.  Called by the review UI on skip-toggle in place of PATCHing OpenRegister's relation endpoint directly. Skipping a prohibition-matched entity is rejected with HTTP 422 (absolute at/above the threshold; below it only unless `force`). Include / non-skip decisions are always allowed and forwarded to OpenRegister.  `$id` is a caller-supplied primary key into a table that is NOT scoped to the caller, so the decision path is authorised twice: authentication here, and per-document ownership inside RelationSkipDecisionService (which is where the relation, and therefore its Nextcloud file id, is loaded). A relation on a document the caller cannot reach yields the same 404 as one that does not exist.

post.description: Create a new consent request for a detected entity  Idempotent on `(documentId, entityKey, scope: "document")`. The service reports which branch it took through `wasUpdated`; the status line MUST agree with it. HTTP 201 is reserved for "a new resource was created" (RFC 9110 §15.3.2), so an idempotent re-submit, which creates nothing, answers 200. Before this fix the controller returned a hardcoded 201 while the very same body said `wasUpdated: true`.

post.summary: Generate a single document from a template
post.description: Generate a single document from a template.  POST /api/documents/generate  Request body: - templateId (string, required): UUID of the template - dataRefs (array, required): [{register, schema, id}, ...] - options (object, optional): format, huisstijlId, zaakId, adHocData, listRefs, pdfOptions, output - listRefs (array, optional): [{register, schema, filter?, limit?, order?, as?}, ...], each resolves to an array of objects in the Twig context under key 'as' (default: schema + '_list') - output (object, optional): {mode?: 'return'|'files'|'both', targetPath?}, defaults to mode 'return' (byte-identical to omitting it). 'files' stores the document in the requesting user's Files and returns JSON refs instead of a binary; 'both' stores AND returns the binary, with the stored file identified via X-Docudesk-File-Id/X-Docudesk-File-Path response headers. - filename (string, optional): Download filename (also used as the stored filename's basename when output.mode is 'files'/'both')

200.description: Generated document binary, 	 *                                           stored-file JSON refs, or error

delete.description: Delete a prohibition.  `publicationProhibition` declares `x-openregister-archival` in `lib/Settings/filinq_register.json` (retention P10Y, prohibitions are court-order-backed and must survive for audit and appeal). OpenRegister therefore refuses EVERY user-driven delete on this schema: rows expire only through `OCA\OpenRegister\BackgroundJob\ArchivalRetentionTask`. The endpoint is consequently impossible to satisfy, never merely "currently failing", and previously leaked that as an opaque HTTP 500.  It now answers HTTP 409 Conflict: the request conflicts with the resource's declared retention state, and no retry, permission change or payload change can make it succeed. The body names retention as the reason and carries OpenRegister's own `SCHEMA_ARCHIVAL_IMMUTABLE` discriminator so a client can tell this apart from the 403 the permission gate raises.
